question: What is the biggest secret you are keeping from your own family?
story: I accidentally became my own parents' landlord, and five years later they still have no idea. It started when their house slipped into foreclosure. I had just sold a tiny app for a decent chunk of money, more than a broke twenty-four-year-old knew what to do with. So I quietly bought their house at auction through a little company with the most boring name I could invent. Then I hired a property manager to rent it right back to them for suspiciously cheap. My parents think some kind investor swooped in to save them. Every month they mail their rent to a PO box. That PO box is me. I use their rent to secretly cover the property taxes and fix the leaky roof. My dad brags to the neighbors about his amazing landlord who never raises the rent. I just smile and nod. One day I will hand them the deed. Until then, I am the best landlord they will never meet.
